text:
marisol: Want to capture the intake -> deferred-bench pattern we discussed. Proposal: do minimal synchronous checks at ingest (tokenizer roundtrip, single forward, small "fast-probe" of ~40 golden prompts) and then put the model into `held_for_verification` while a full bench job runs async. If bench passes, we move to `shadowing` and then a staged canary.

dan: Sounds reasonable. Key wants: reduce wasted bench cycles, but avoid having bad models serve traffic. How long can a model live in `held_for_verification`? We should forbid routing until at least shadowing starts.

anya: My take: lifecycle states (simple names): ingested -> prelim_ok -> held_for_verification -> shadowing -> promoted OR quarantined OR rejected. Each state has TTLs: prelim_ok (48h max before bench scheduled), held_for_verification (72h max before auto-stale -> manual review), shadowing (24h) -> promoted. Also add an explicit `stale` tag used by ops.

marisol: Good. Also: the fast-probe should be intentionally coarse to avoid false rejects. It should catch mismatched tokenizers, missing special tokens, wrong EOS handling, and obvious shape errors. Bench should do strict regression checks.

sysops: Operational constraints: - org-level bench quota (GPU-hours/day) - per-candidate max GPU-hours - queue priority tiers (enterprise > paid > free) - pending-time cutoff (if candidate pending > TTL, mark stale and notify owner). If bench hits quota, intake should mark candidate `queued_for_manual` and block promotion.

bench-bot: New bench job enqueued: candidate=cand-1767771234, est_gpu_hours=2.6, expected_completion=~5h; webhook=/hooks/bench/result. Current bench queue depth=4.

dan: What does the bench webhook look like? We need a compact payload so we don't send huge artifacts in the notification. Proposal (keys only): candidate_id, verdict(enum: pass|flag|critical), failed_check_ids[], drift_score (0-1), p95_ms, golden_set_ref, bench_run_id, summary_url. Example payload:```json
{"candidate_id":"cand-1767771234","verdict":"flag","failed_check_ids":["regression:qa-v6"],"drift_score":"0.28","p95_ms":"295","golden_set_ref":"gold-2026-03-05-v2","bench_run_id":"bench-4521","summary_url":"https://bench.internal/r/bench-4521"}```

anya: Intake should accept the webhook and translate bench verdicts into actions: pass -> schedule shadowing, flag -> set quarantined_with_details and trigger auto-notify + attach artifacts, critical -> immediate rollback if any traffic routed + create P0 incident. Also the webhook handler should record golden_set_ref into the model metadata and fail if mismatch with candidate metadata.

marisol: On rollout, require shadowing first (no responses returned to users, but collect latency/usage). Then a canary stage: route 0.05% for 30m, 0.5% for 1h, 2% for 2h, then promote. Any bench veto during these steps forces immediate halt and rollback.

sysops: Edge rules: - If bench job doesn't complete within bench_TTL (configurable, default 48h), set candidate->stale and open manual review ticket. - Provide an org-level "fast-pass" budget for emergency approvals (audit trail required). - Allow owners to cancel bench jobs; cancelled candidates become rejected unless opted otherwise.

dan: Prefilter idea: run a tokenization hash + embedding sanity check in intake to filter obvious mismatches before enqueueing expensive bench runs. That should save a lot. Also keep a tiny "smoke golden" (40-60 items) and a mapping of which golden_set_ref was used for smoke.

bench-bot: Bench verdict posted for cand-1767771234: verdict=flag, failed_check_ids=["regression:qa-v6"], drift_score=0.31, p95_ms=310, golden_set_ref=gold-2026-03-05-v2, bench_run_id=bench-4521, summary_url=https://bench.internal/r/bench-4521

anya: On a flagged verdict we should: 1) move candidate to `quarantined`, 2) stop any ongoing canaries, 3) surface diffs in console and attach summary_url, 4) notify owner + SRE, 5) optionally allow owner to request rebench with different golden_set or updated model.

marisol: We also need to version golden artifacts carefully. Model metadata should include: {"golden_set_ref":"string","golden_probe_hash":"hex"} and bench must echo golden_set_ref. Runtime behavior: when routing, runtime should verify model metadata includes golden_set_ref; if missing, reject model from being promoted.

dan: Add monitoring hooks: track time-in-state metrics, bench queue latency, per-org bench spend, and number of quarantines per org. These should feed a weekly report and alert if quarantines spike > threshold.

sysops: I'll draft the operational knobs and the circuit-breaker behavior for quota exhaustion. Also will add a runbook: manual requeue, manual approval flow, and what to do if bench artifacts are unavailable.

anya: I'll synthesize this into a short RFC: state machine diagram, webhook schema, TTLs, bench quotas, prefilter heuristics, and rollout recipe. Want reviewers: marisol for onboarding UX, dan for state machine, sysops for ops controls, bench infra for payload schema.

marisol: I'll review and add the fast-probe set.

bench-bot: Note: median bench wait is 1.2h, mean run time 4.8h.

anya: Thanks — aiming to post the RFC tomorrow morning.
